tools.name: create-markdown-at-path
tools.description:
Create a node path if missing and write markdown content at the target node.

  This tool guarantees the target path exists by creating any missing nodes along the way,
  including new top-level sections under a person when needed.

  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  🛠️ CREATE-OR-WRITE PATH TOOL
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  BEHAVIOR:
  - If all path nodes already exist, it updates the target node content
  - If one or more path nodes are missing, it creates them first
  - Then it replaces all children under the target node with the provided markdown

  PATH FORMAT:
  - Array of strings representing the navigation path
  - Path must not be empty
  - Matching is tolerant for common variants
  - Missing segments are created with the exact names provided

  USAGE EXAMPLES:
  - Create a top-level section:
    path = ["Roadmap"]
  - Create nested path:
    path = ["Exploration", "Q2 Themes", "AI Ops"]
  - Create Brainlift branch:
    path = ["BrainLifts", "Brainlift 9: New Topic", "DOK4 - SPOV"]

  SAFETY:
  - Full-person replacement is not allowed
  - Only the target node's children are replaced
  - Other parts of the person's structure remain untouched

departmentName.description: Department name (must be verified to exist)

personName.description: Person name (must be verified to exist in the department)

path.description: Array of node names representing the path to create/use. Must not be empty.

markdown.description: Markdown content to set at the target path after path creation.

tools.name: get-brainlift-section
tools.description:
Read a specific section from a Brainlift structure.
  
  This tool is specifically designed for reading Brainlift documents and provides
  easy access to individual sections without needing to specify full paths.
  
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  🧠 BRAINLIFT SECTION READER
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  
  SUPPORTED SECTIONS:
  - "Owner" - List of brainlift owners/contributors
  - "Purpose" - Primary purpose and out-of-scope items  
  - "DOK4 - SPOV" - Spiky Points of View
  - "DOK3 - Insights" - Key insights derived from knowledge
  - "Experts" - Domain experts with structured profiles
  - "DOK2 - Knowledge Tree" - Categorized sources with facts and summaries
  
  USAGE:
  - Specify section to get just that section
  - Leave section empty to get entire Brainlift content
  
  AUTOMATIC PATH CONSTRUCTION:
  The tool automatically constructs the path: ["Brainlifts", brainliftName, section]
  
  EXAMPLES:
  - Get SPOV section: section = "DOK4 - SPOV"
  - Get all experts: section = "Experts"  
  - Get entire brainlift: section = "" (empty)

brainliftName.description: Name of the Brainlift (e.g., 'Brainlift 1: Creating a Successful Channel-First GTM')

section.description: Brainlift section to read. Leave empty to get entire Brainlift content.

tools.name: get-markdown-at-path
tools.description:
Get markdown content from a specific path within a person's WorkFlowy structure.
  
  This tool allows you to read content from specific sub-nodes within a person's second brain,
  rather than getting their entire content.
  
  USAGE EXAMPLES:

  For this structure:
  1. Jane Doe
     1.1. Brainlifts
          1.1.1. Brainlift 1: Project Alpha
          1.1.2. Brainlift 2: Market Research Strategy
     1.2. Exploration
          1.2.1. Emerging Brainlifts
          1.2.2. Sandbox

  Examples:
  - To get all Brainlifts: path = ["Brainlifts"]
  - To get specific Brainlift: path = ["Brainlifts", "Brainlift 1: Project Alpha"]
  - To get Exploration content: path = ["Exploration"]
  - To get Emerging Brainlifts: path = ["Exploration", "Emerging Brainlifts"]
  - To get entire person content: path = [] (empty array)
  
  PATH FORMAT:
  - Array of strings representing the navigation path
  - Each string should match the exact name of the node
  - Path is case-sensitive and must match exactly
  - Empty path [] returns the entire person's content

path.description: Array of node names representing the path to navigate. Use empty array [] to get entire person content.

tools.name: set-brainlift-section
tools.description:
Update a specific section within a Brainlift structure.
  
  This tool is specifically designed for editing Brainlift documents and provides
  built-in validation and structure guidance for each section type.
  
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  🧠 BRAINLIFT SECTION EDITOR
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  
  SUPPORTED SECTIONS:
  - "Owner" - List of brainlift owners/contributors
  - "Purpose" - Primary purpose and out-of-scope items  
  - "DOK4 - SPOV" - Spiky Points of View (sharp, defensible viewpoints)
  - "DOK3 - Insights" - Key insights derived from knowledge
  - "Experts" - Domain experts with structured profiles
  - "DOK2 - Knowledge Tree" - Categorized sources with facts and summaries
  
  SECTION-SPECIFIC VALIDATION:
  
  Owner Section:
  * Should contain names in bullet point format
  * Example: "* John Doe
* Jane Smith"
  
  Purpose Section:
  * Should include both primary purpose and out-of-scope items
  * Example: "* Primary: Develop GTM strategy
* Out of scope: Implementation details"
  
  DOK4 - SPOV Section:
  * Should contain spiky, provocative viewpoints
  * Must be defensible, challenging, and memorable
  * Should be polarizing (people love it or hate it)
  
  DOK3 - Insights Section:
  * Should contain interpretative observations
  * More than summaries - thematic insights from data
  
  Experts Section:
  * Each expert must have: who, focus, why follow, where
  * Example structure:
    "* Expert 1:
       * who: Title and credentials
       * focus: Areas of expertise  
       * why follow: Their relevance to this brainlift
       * where: Twitter, LinkedIn, blog URLs"
  
  DOK2 - Knowledge Tree Section:
  * Should contain categories with sources
  * Each source needs: DOK1 facts, DOK2 summary, links
  * Example structure:
    "* Category 1:
       * Source 1:
         * DOK1 - facts:
           * Fact 1
           * Fact 2
         * DOK2 - summary:
           * Summary point 1
         * link: https://example.com"
  
  AUTOMATIC PATH CONSTRUCTION:
  The tool automatically constructs the path: ["Brainlifts", brainliftName, section]
  
  VALIDATION & FEEDBACK:
  - Provides real-time validation for section structure
  - Suggests improvements for content quality
  - Warns about missing required elements
  - Offers formatting guidance

departmentName.description: Department name (must be verified to exist)

personName.description: Person name (must be verified to exist in the department)

brainliftName.description: Name of the Brainlift (e.g., 'Brainlift 1: Creating a Successful Channel-First GTM')

section.description: Brainlift section to update. Must be one of the predefined section types.

content.description: Markdown content for the section. Will be validated against section-specific requirements.

tools.name: set-markdown-at-path
tools.description:
Update markdown content at a specific path within a person's WorkFlowy structure.
  
  This tool allows you to update content in specific sub-nodes within a person's second brain,
  without affecting other parts of their structure.
  
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  ⚠️  TARGETED CONTENT REPLACEMENT ⚠️
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  
  THIS TOOL REPLACES ALL CONTENT UNDER THE SPECIFIED PATH NODE.
  
  This only affects the target node and its children,
  leaving the rest of the person's structure intact.
  
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  🧠 BRAINLIFT STRUCTURE SUPPORT
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  
  This tool has built-in support for Brainlift structures. Common Brainlift sections:
  
  BRAINLIFT SECTION EXAMPLES:
  - Update Owner section: path = ["Brainlifts", "Brainlift Name", "Owner"]
  - Update Purpose: path = ["Brainlifts", "Brainlift Name", "Purpose"] 
  - Update DOK4 SPOVs: path = ["Brainlifts", "Brainlift Name", "DOK4 - SPOV"]
  - Update DOK3 Insights: path = ["Brainlifts", "Brainlift Name", "DOK3 - Insights"]
  - Update Experts: path = ["Brainlifts", "Brainlift Name", "Experts"]
  - Update Knowledge Tree: path = ["Brainlifts", "Brainlift Name", "DOK2 - Knowledge Tree"]
  - Update specific category: path = ["Brainlifts", "Brainlift Name", "DOK2 - Knowledge Tree", "Category 1"]
  - Update specific expert: path = ["Brainlifts", "Brainlift Name", "Experts", "Expert 1"]
  
  GENERAL STRUCTURE EXAMPLES:
  - Update specific Brainlift: path = ["Brainlifts", "Brainlift 1: Creating a Successful Channel-First GTM"]
  - Update Emerging Brainlifts: path = ["Exploration", "Emerging Brainlifts"]
  - Update Sandbox: path = ["Exploration", "Sandbox"]
  
  BRAINLIFT CONTENT VALIDATION:
  The tool will provide helpful feedback if your content doesn't follow Brainlift structure:
  - Owner section should contain names
  - Purpose should have primary purpose and out of scope
  - DOK4 should contain Spiky Points of View (SPOVs)
  - DOK3 should contain insights
  - Experts should follow the 4-point structure (who, focus, why follow, where)
  - Knowledge Tree should have proper DOK1/DOK2 structure with sources
  
  WORKFLOW:
  1. Use get-markdown-at-path to see current content at the target path
  2. Modify the content following Brainlift structure guidelines
  3. Use this tool to update only that specific path
  
  PATH FORMAT:
  - Array of strings representing the navigation path
  - Each string should match the exact name of the node
  - Path is case-sensitive and must match exactly
  - Path must not be empty
  
  SAFETY:
  - Always verify the path exists using get-markdown-at-path first
  - Only the content under the specified path will be replaced
  - Other parts of the person's structure remain untouched

departmentName.description: Department name (must be verified to exist)

personName.description: Person name (must be verified to exist in the department)

path.description: Array of node names representing the path to the target node. Must not be empty.

markdown.description: Markdown content to set at the specified path. This will replace all existing content under the target node.
